From the filled 115.00 entry, the 180.00 target against an 82.00 bear case is 65/33 = **1.97:1, against the 2.5 floor for long_term** — the same failure as today's NKE row and yesterday's LCII, and for the same structural reason: three consumer-discretionary long_term longs were entered 11-12% above where they now trade, carry no stop of any kind, and cannot be made to clear their floors without a bear case above where a broken brand would actually trade. Conviction is cut to 2 to match what the evidence supports, and the size with it.
key_risk: A conviction-2 idea and it must be read as one: the supporting evidence is a single technical level and nothing else — no insider buying, no dated catalyst, no valuation work I could defend today, and no stop. LULU closed 101.30, 25.59% off its 136.14 high and only 6.2% above its 90-day low of 95.35, below SMA20 105.13 and SMA50 113.73, in the weakest part of the tape (XLY -9.5% off its high, XRT -11.8%, both below both averages). INVALIDATION, replacing the stop it has never had: comparable-store sales negative for two consecutive quarters, OR gross margin below 55% for two consecutive quarters, OR a monthly close below the 95.35 low. Any one of those means the de-rating is structural and the position closes regardless of the 180.00 target. MECHANICAL NOTE: state also carries a filled LULU SELL row at 100.61 from the 2026-09-08 exit recommendation, so this name is tracked as two positions from one view — flagged, not fixed here.
counter_argument: The bull case is that a premium brand with this gross-margin profile does not permanently de-rate 25% on a soft consumer, and that buying it 6% off the low in a hiking cycle is exactly when multi-year positions are built. I cannot rebut that, and it may well be right. What I can say is that it is not supported by anything I fetched today — there is no insider buying underneath it, no revision inflection, and no valuation number I derived rather than assumed. An unsupported bull case is a conviction 2, not a reason to add.

thesis: Close it while it is free to close. key_risk: This closes a position that is not losing, in a company that beat three of its last four prints (+30.8%, +18.3%, +47.2%, -15.9%), which is a real cost if the housing read is wrong. It is also thinly traded relative to the rest of the book at $23M/day, so exit should be worked rather than dumped at the open print. The honest counterweight: BCC is 12.77% off its high but still only slightly below SMA50 79.16 and sitting on SMA20 76.59 — this is a pre-emptive exit on the driver, not a reaction to a breakdown, and pre-emptive exits are wrong more often than reactive ones.
counter_argument: Building products are cyclical and the time to own them is when rates are high and starts are depressed, not after the recovery is obvious — so closing here could be selling the bottom of the cycle. The answer is that nothing in the data says this is the bottom: the Fed hiked twelve days ago with 16 of 18 participants projecting another, the long end is still rising rather than anticipating relief, there is zero insider buying against $666K of sells, and analyst revisions are flat rather than inflecting. A cyclical bottom normally shows at least one of those turning first. When one does, BCC can be re-entered with the stop it has never had.

counter_argument: The case for closing now rather than waiting is strong — at 0.92 ATR the stop will most likely fire within days, and taking -2.9% by hand beats -4.9% at the stop. I am not taking it, for the same reason CCJ is held and CAG is not: the stop sits under a real level (SMA50) rather than inside the noise, so it exits at a price chosen in advance. Closing by hand would also be a third exit today on top of CAG and BCC, and cutting three positions in one session because a correlation counter is uncomfortable is its own error — the cap should bind on new exposure, which is what the four order cancellations do.
